issues.description: Method Lecture.getTotalNumberOfStudents(): the problem statement (UML) declares getTotalNumberOfStudents() with return type int, but the solution implementation declares public StudentCount getTotalNumberOfStudents() and returns a StudentCount instance. The template contains a TODO for implementing getTotalNumberOfStudents() and therefore implies the UML signature (int). This mismatch means students following the UML/template will expect an int-returning method while the provided solution and additional StudentCount class use a different return type, causing compilation/test signature incompatibilities and confusion about the intended API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Preferred option (align with UML/template): change Lecture.getTotalNumberOfStudents() in the solution to return an int (sum of inscribed and guest students) and remove or stop using the StudentCount class; update dependent methods (getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents and getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor) to use the int value. Concretely: replace public StudentCount getTotalNumberOfStudents() { return new StudentCount(...); } with public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() { return numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents; } and delete StudentCount.java. Alternative option (if StudentCount is intended): update the problem statement and UML to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents(): StudentCount and add StudentCount.java to the template repository so template, UML, and solution match.

issues.description: Concept: total number of students for a Lecture. Problem statement / UML and the template indicate a method getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns an int (the UML shows +getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int and the task text describes returning the total number of students). In the solution, getTotalNumberOfStudents() is implemented to return a StudentCount object (class StudentCount) rather than an int. This introduces a new identifier (StudentCount) and changes the expected return type for the same conceptual entity. A student reading the UML and template would expect to implement/consume an int-returning method, but the solution (and provided StudentCount class) uses a different type and identifier, which breaks the direct mapping between requirement and implementation and may confuse or block students.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representation consistent across artifacts. Preferred fixes: (A) Align to the problem/UML by changing the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (sum of inscribed and guest students) and remove the StudentCount wrapper class, updating any call sites accordingly; or (B) If the StudentCount wrapper is intentional, update the problem statement, UML, and template to declare and document the StudentCount type and specify getTotalNumberOfStudents(): StudentCount so the identifier and return type match across all artifacts.
